title: Grok returns a list of matches for repeated pattern names #92092

timeline.message:
Grok returns a list of matches for repeated pattern names #92092

This commit makes the Elasticsearch Grok processor behaves the same that
Logstash's grok:

when Logstash's Grok processor runs with a pattern having repeated 
pattern names (e.g.: `"%{IP:ip} %{IP:ip} %{anything else}"`), it returns
a list of matches, instead only the first match. 

Closes #92092
timeline.author: Pablo Alcantar Morales

timeline.body:
This commit makes the Elasticsearch Grok processor behaves the same that Logstash's grok:

when Logstash's Grok processor runs with a pattern having repeated pattern names (e.g.: `"%{IP:ip} %{IP:ip} %{anything else}"`), it returns a list of matches, instead only the first match. 

Closes #92092
Pinging @elastic/es-data-management (Team:Data Management)
I've decided to use this type of `Map` since otherwise, the code becomes a bit messy while extracting the elements

reply.body:
I see, do you think we could implement this maybe earlier in the process? In the emission of the values maybe? This is just an idea to discuss where it's better to implement this.

I am trying to consider also the performance a bit, adding it here adds a small penalty to every grok processor. I was hoping if we did it closer to the emission we could check if there are multiple entries and only use a list there.

Let me know what you think. I haven't worked  on the solution by the way, I am just sharing my thoughts on the subject and I think it might be worth a small effort to see if it's possible.

This is the earlier stage where this can happen because within the `Grok` class we never traverse the list of (potential) captured groups. Thinking about the performance, I had an idea to avoid having to reserve memory in case a group is only being used once (-> do not have to create an ArrayList with 1 element). I'll the update the PR tomorrow

timeline.author: Pablo Alcantar Morales

timeline.body: Usually we used `ignored` rather than something like `__` for this.

+[[eql-samples]]
+=== Samples
+
+You can use EQL samples to describe and match a chronologically unordered series
+of events. All events in a sample share the same value for one or more fields
+that are specified using the <<eql-by-keyword,`by` keyword>> (join keys). Each
+item in a sample is an event category and event condition, surrounded by square
+brackets (`[ ]`). Events are listed in the order of the filters they match.
+
+[source,eql]
+----
+sample by join_key
+  [ event_category_1 where condition_1 ]
+  [ event_category_2 where condition_2 ]
+  ...
+----
+
+*Example* + 
+The following EQL sample query returns up to 10 samples with unique values for
+`host`. Each sample consists of two events:
+
+. Start with an event with:
++
+--
+* An event category of `file`
+* A `file.extension` of `exe`
+--
+. Followed by an event with an event category of `process`
+
+[source,eql]
+----
+sample by host
+  [ file where file.extension == "exe" ]
+  [ process where true ]
+----
+
+Sample queries do not take into account the chronological ordering of events.
+The `with maxspan` and `with runs` statements as well as the `until` keyword are
+not supported.

+
+NOTE: The precision field does not result in a distance match.
+Specifying a distance value like `10km` only results in a geohash precision value that represents tiles of that size.
+The precision will be used to encode the search geo point into a geohash tile for completion matching.
+A consequence of this is that points outside that tile, even if very close to the search point, will not be matched.
+Reducing the precision, or increasing the distance, can reduce the risk of this happening, but not entirely remove it.
